response.sql: SELECT player_id, SUM(triple) AS total_triples FROM batting_postseason WHERE player_id IN (SELECT player_id FROM batting_postseason WHERE league_id = 'NL' AND round = 'WS') GROUP BY player_id ORDER BY total_triples DESC, player_id ASC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The total covers all of a qualifying player's postseason batting records (every round and league), as requested. Only the qualification test uses the NL and WS filter.
Ties in the total are broken by player_id ascending, so the top 10 is deterministic. The request doesn't specify a tie-break.

A player whose triple values are all NULL gets a NULL total. SQLite sorts NULLs first in descending order, so the query's DESC ordering would put them first. With the columns as defined (triple is INTEGER), NULLs are unlikely to appear, but the request asks for missing totals last.

alternatives.interpretation: Same query, but with an explicit NULLS LAST so any missing totals sort last, as the request asks.
